clue.text: Constant crazy fads in bad taste

indicators.note: something crazy is wild and disordered, so the first set of letters is jumbled
bad here means spoilt or out of shape, telling us the second word is rearranged too

explanation.surface: A critic sneers that ever-changing fads are in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words go into one combined anagram, each with its own signal: crazy fads and bad taste give STEADFAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone steadfast is loyal and unwavering, the same idea as constant in its sense of faithful.

clue.text: Crowd's friendly

parts.note: a warm welcome is a friendly one

explanation.walkthrough: The 's looks like a possessive or 'is', but it simply provides the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a dense, moving mass of people or insects, so it is a synonym for a crowd.

clue.text: Way to pursue English maiden requires courage ultimately to share feelings

indicators.note: to pursue is to chase after, so this word goes behind the following pieces

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
read loosely as 'is', as in 'is needing'

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A romantic advice column: the path to winning an English girl takes some nerve in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: E, M, PATH, IS and E give EMPATHISE; the IS from 'requires' is the setter's loose stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To empathise is to understand and share another person's emotions, which is sharing feelings.

clue.text: In the period around Christmas, the French board of fare's scrumptious

indicators.note: In tells us one piece sits inside the period that follows it

parts.note: the calendar abbreviation for December, the month Christmas falls in
the table is the board on which food is served

explanation.surface: Over the festive season, the French spread on the table is delicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' is an old word for a dining table, as in 'bed and board', and 'board of fare' plays on 'bill of fare', a menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectable food is delicious and highly pleasing, matching scrumptious as a synonym.

clue.text: Forgive drunken slob in prayer

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for a prayer

parts.note: an Ave Maria is a prayer to the Virgin Mary

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so these letters lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: A priest is asked to pardon a drunk lout who is mid-prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to free someone from guilt or sin, which is to forgive them.

clue.text: Persecution of alleged arsonist

indicators.note: alleged means said to be, so we want something that is only said, as a sound

parts.note: an arsonist torches buildings, so is a torcher

explanation.surface: A report on the harassment of a suspected fire-raiser.
explanation.walkthrough: A torcher, one who sets fires, is pronounced just like the answer in a British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Torture is the deliberate infliction of pain, the extreme form of persecuting someone.

clue.text: Part of motor I've tried to fix has …

indicators.note: Part of says the letters lie inside a run of the clue's own words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A mechanic begins describing a bit of engine they tried to repair, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 9 across in the surface only; 'has' is padding for that join.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet is to fasten with metal bolts, so it means fix in the sense of attach firmly.

clue.text: Defeat of king exposed

parts.note: R for Rex, Latin for king
a secret that is out is exposed

explanation.surface: A monarch is beaten and his weakness laid bare.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing, disorderly defeat in battle or competition.

clue.text: Watch as Dante's companion runs out

indicators.note: out means leaving, so the letter for runs is taken away

parts.note: the Roman poet guides Dante through Hell in the Inferno
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a lookout as Dante's guide hurries away.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from VIRGIL to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of staying awake to keep watch, so the noun watch is a synonym.

clue.text: Note to Father: "Now going out; bring cuddly toy!

parts.note: te is a note in the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: going out means leaving, so those letters are removed from the father word

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, the present era
to bear is to carry or bring

explanation.surface: A child leaves a note for Dad on the way out, asking him to fetch a soft toy.
explanation.walkthrough: AD leaves DADDY to give DDY. AD stands for now because it marks the current era of the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is a stuffed toy bear that children hug, so it is an example of a cuddly toy.

clue.text: … Dad turning to friend with dismay!

indicators.note: turning means facing round, so the word for dad is read backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a pal is a friend; to marks it as following

explanation.surface: Continuing 6 across: Dad turns to a friend in horror.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock and horrify, which is a strong way to dismay someone.

clue.text: Cadged drugs once at work

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being reshaped, so they form a new word

explanation.surface: Someone admits they used to beg for narcotics in the office.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge is to get something by begging or borrowing without paying, which is to cadge it.

clue.text: Fastidious London police have one copper on bug detail

indicators.note: read as de-tail, removing the tail, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Police
a louse is a bug; on means it comes next

explanation.surface: The Met assigns one officer to a surveillance-bug job, and is fussy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman in this surface but is the metal. LOUSE loses its tail to leave LOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Meticulous means showing great attention to precision, the same as fastidious or very careful.

clue.text: Love to take part in lavish stratagem

indicators.note: taking part in something means being inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to ply someone with food or drink is to lavish it on them
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: An extravagant scheme someone would love to join.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploy is a cunning manoeuvre to gain an advantage, which is what a stratagem is.

clue.text: Cooked supper may include delightful finale with sweet sauce

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so these letters are mixed up
include adds the selected letter to the mix before it is rearranged
the finale is the closing part, so only the end letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A meal promises a lovely ending: something sweet poured on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple syrup is a sweet syrup from maple sap, poured over pancakes like a dessert topping.

clue.text: Rattle reservists following a soldier on initial training exercise

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the reservists sit behind the soldier

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the TA was the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: initial means first, so only the opening letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Part-time soldiers on a training exercise shake up a regular.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to disturb or unsettle someone, which is what rattling them means.

clue.text: One starts fight with Georgia over good brand of petrol to go in Rolls-Royce

indicators.note: over in a down clue means flipped upwards, so the state abbreviation reads backwards
to go in means to be placed inside, so the petrol brand sits within the car initials

parts.note: Esso is a well-known fuel brand

explanation.surface: Someone picks a fight about which fuel goes in a Rolls-Royce in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgia' could be the country, but the US state abbreviation is what is needed; Esso is a petrol brand familiar in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressor is the party that attacks first or starts hostilities.

clue.text: Question former dictator on end of regime

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, so ex means former
Idi Amin, the dictator of Uganda

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Interrogating an ex-tyrant about the collapse of his rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine a witness is to question them closely, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Home education leads to instinctive understanding

explanation.surface: A claim that home-schooling breeds gut feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition is knowing something immediately without conscious reasoning, an instinctive grasp.

clue.text: Girl men fancy is a mischievous creature

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or imaginative, so these letters take a new form

explanation.surface: The girl all the men are keen on turns out to be a little imp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as the verb 'to be attracted to', but it is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary sprite blamed for mechanical faults, a small troublemaking being.

clue.text: Candidate opposed to coal for energy?

parts.note: coal comes from a mine, and a coal mine is called simply a mine

explanation.surface: Asking whether an election candidate is against burning coal for power.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward for an office or award, so a candidate.

clue.text: Support overthrow of heartless Stuart Queen

indicators.note: the word splits as over plus throw, and over means turned back, so the throwing word is read in reverse

parts.note: to lob is to throw high

indicators.note: heartless means the centre is removed, so only the outside letters stay

explanation.surface: Backing the overthrow of a cruel Stuart queen, perhaps Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overthrow' looks like one word meaning to topple, but splits into over (reverse) and throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster is to prop up or reinforce, so it is a synonym of the verb support.

clue.text: Cats from Myanmar?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a breed of short-haired domestic cat
second meaning: belonging to the country formerly called Burma

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as asking for cats native to Myanmar; the word means both the cat breed and the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed name and the adjective for the country's people are the same word, from the country's old name.

clue.text: Sailing boat doesn't begin to impress

indicators.note: doesn't begin means its first letter is missing

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A yacht fails to make a good first impression.
explanation.walkthrough: KETCH loses its K. 'Impress' here means to imprint, not to wow.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave a design into a surface, which is to impress it in the sense of stamp.

clue.text: Grovel to Conservative overlord

indicators.note: the word splits as over plus lord, and over in a down clue means turned upwards, so the nobleman word reads backwards

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A Tory toadies up to his boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlord' looks like one word for a boss, but splits into over (reverse) and lord.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to behave obsequiously to win favour, which is grovelling.

clue.text: I get male to iron one very easy top — amazing!

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across clue is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of getting a man to iron a simple shirt, which is astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as a garment to be ironed, but takes the first letter of 'easy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Impressive means striking enough to inspire admiration, close to amazing.

clue.text: Keen to agree for a change

indicators.note: for a change means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone usually contrary is happy to say yes for once.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eager means being enthusiastic and willing, a direct synonym of keen.

clue.text: Hut in Slough

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a simple garden outbuilding
second meaning: to cast off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the town west of London, but here it is the verb to cast off skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a small wooden hut, while the verb means to discard skin, as a snake does when sloughing.

clue.text: Penny, in haste, forced drug on another girl

indicators.note: forced means pushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A girl called Penny hurriedly pushes drugs on another girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like the first girl's name, but it is the coin. The jumbled letters are followed by E.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephanie is a girl's name, and 'another' refers back to Penny, which reads as a name too.

clue.text: Regretting group's about-turn

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the group word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a ring is a group, as of criminals

explanation.surface: Remorse over a band's sudden reversal of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About-turn' looks like one phrase, but splits into about (container) and turn (U).
explanation.definitionFit: Ruing is the present participle of rue, to feel sorry about something, so regretting.

clue.text: Speedy capture of President in attack

indicators.note: a capture holds something inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: A swift strike to seize a head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means happening or moving quickly, a direct synonym of speedy.

clue.text: Surprising sight of me reportedly batting first

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the pronoun for myself said out loud
the opener is the cricketer who bats first

explanation.surface: The amazing spectacle of the narrator going in first in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opening batsman, the opener, starts the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is something revealing or astonishing, so a startling spectacle fits.
